transcript:
00:00:02 Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — Jordan from Redwood. We have Priya and Alex as well, Priya's our security-focused SE. Samira: you on?
00:00:07 Samira (Acme CISO): Yeah hi, thanks. Got a fair agenda — IR, BCDR, SLA specifics, that sort of thing.
00:00:15 Priya (Redwood SE): Hi all. Quick note — we'll try to cover SOC 2 and ISO artifacts briefly, then dive into RTO/RPO and escalation diagrams. We'll also map to our Dedicated/Private options.
00:00:28 Luis (Head of Infra): Important for us: if something goes down, we need to know how quickly stateful services recover and what the data loss window is. So RTO and RPO, please.
00:00:40 Alex (Redwood): Yep. Also, we'll show how audit logs and KMS tie into that — key rotation, HSM, that flow.
00:00:47 Tom (SRE): We run multiple clusters, some EU-only due to residency. Want to confirm data-at-rest encryption and key ownership options.
00:00:55 Priya: Understood. To start, SOC 2: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II — we can share the report. For ISO, we maintain ISO 27001 controls; again we'll share the certificate and scope doc. Some of those artifacts are redacted in parts but should be useful.
00:01:12 Samira: Good. Please include scope — particularly Dedicated vs Hosted and Private control plane differences.
00:01:19 Jordan: Sure. We'll annotate which controls apply to each deployment mode.
00:01:25 Priya: On RBAC and SSO — we support SAML 2.0/IdP integrations, SCIM provisioning, and role-based access controls with granular roles. There are default roles and you can create custom roles.
00:01:40 Luis: Any limit on SCIM provisioning? We expect 3k users eventually.
00:01:44 Priya: SCIM scales; we've onboarded orgs at that scale. There might be rate-limiting during initial syncs but we have recommended sync windows in the docs. We'll include that note.
00:01:56 Tom: Audit logs — retention defaults and options? We have retention policies for 1 year for infra logs, 7 years for compliance in some contexts.
00:02:06 Alex: Default audit log retention is 90 days in the hosted plane, but for Dedicated and Private you control retention — we can push logs to your SIEM or S3 with configurable TTLs. We'll also include a link to our log export docs.
00:02:21 Samira: Can logs be forwarded real-time to our Splunk? We want immutability guarantees.
00:02:27 Priya: Yes, we support streaming audit events to your SIEM. Immutability depends on the destination; we sign logs and include sequence numbers, and we can enable write-once objects in your bucket or use your append-only store. We'll add specifics.
00:02:44 Luis: KMS — do you use customer-managed keys or Redwood-managed? What's rotation policy and HSM usage?
00:02:51 Alex: For Hosted by default Redwood-managed. For Dedicated/Private we support customer-managed keys via KMS — Google KMS, AWS KMS, or wrapped keys in an HSM. Rotation is configurable; we recommend 90-day rotation for data encryption keys and we log all key usage by principal.
00:03:08 Tom: Do you have an option for an on-prem HSM?
00:03:11 Priya: For Private deployments we can integrate with on-prem HSMs or your KMS over VPN. We'll include a sample architecture showing the key handshake.
00:03:20 Samira: OK good. Let's pivot to incident response and BCDR. We need RTO / RPO targets and examples.
00:03:27 Jordan: For the hosted API our SLA targets are 99.9% for standard tier, higher for Dedicated with contract. But RTO/RPO are more about stateful recovery; Redwood's serving runtime is stateless for inference requests, with KV caches for long-running chat sessions — we persist session state only if you opt in.
00:03:45 Priya: Typical RTO for control plane outages is under 15 minutes with automated failover across regions for critical components; RPO for persistent control plane data is measured in seconds for replicated data, minutes for object store syncs. For Dedicated, recovery is part of the reserved capacity playbook — we commit to faster recovery and a runbook.
00:04:03 Tom: Can you quantify RPO for session KV cache?
00:04:07 Alex: KV cache is in-memory on GPU nodes — unless you enable prefix/KV persistence to S3, RPO is effectively zero (i.e., you lose in-memory cache on node failure). For critical applications we recommend client-side checkpointing or enabling our optional persistence which captures snapshots every X minutes; we can tune snapshot cadence.
00:04:24 Luis: Snapshot cadence? How often?
00:04:27 Priya: Default snapshot cadence is 5 minutes for Dedicated; can go down to 1 minute in high-criticality setups — tradeoff of cost. We'll include cost delta in the follow-up.
00:04:38 Samira: Escalation — what does Redwood's incident escalation chain look like? Our SOC needs 24/7 contact and a documented escalation path to execs.
00:04:48 Jordan: We have a documented escalation matrix: first-line on-call engineers, then SE lead, then engineering manager, then VP of Infra. For Dedicated customers we provide a named CSM and a priority contact plus an escalation SLA. We can provide on-call roster and contact windows.
00:05:03 Tom: Do you have a runbook for sec incidents vs availability incidents?
00:05:07 Priya: Yes - separate IR runbooks. We have playbooks for data exposure, credentials compromise, and availability incidents. Each playbook lists steps for containment, eradication, recovery, notification, and postmortem. Notification templates and regulatory notification timelines are included.
00:05:24 Samira: How do you handle legal/regulatory notification? For GDPR we have 72-hour breach timelines.
00:05:29 Priya: Our playbook includes timelines and we can map our notification steps to your compliance needs; we also maintain audit logs of all communication and actions. For high-severity incidents we'll trigger the legal/exec path and provide a packet for regulators.
00:05:43 Luis: SLA credits — how are they measured and applied?
00:05:46 Jordan: SLA credits are pro-rated based on downtime windows logged against endpoints and the defined measurement points. For Dedicated contracts we can offer higher uptime targets and faster remediation commitments. We'll attach the SLA appendix with the exact formulas.
00:05:59 Tom: Historical uptime? Any dashboard for past 6 months?
00:06:02 Alex: Yes, we can provide a tenant-level uptime report for the last 6-12 months and per-route latency SLAs. We'll include sample metrics in the follow-up.
00:06:12 Samira: Pen testing and vulnerability scanning cadence?
00:06:16 Priya: We run quarterly vulnerability scans and annual third-party pen tests on the control plane. For Dedicated/Private we can coordinate assessments with your pen-test team; we support shared scope agreements.
00:06:28 Luis: What about backup retention and restore testing frequency?
00:06:33 Priya: We snapshot control-plane state nightly and retain backups according to agreed retention — default 30 days for hosted, configurable for Dedicated/Private. We run restore drills quarterly. For customers with strict BCDR we can increase cadence and provide RTO proof points from previous drills.
00:06:49 Samira: Can you share an example postmortem from a restore drill?
00:06:53 Jordan: We'll redact PII but yes, we'll share a sample postmortem showing RTO/RPO achieved and steps taken.
00:06:59 Tom: In terms of escalation latency, what's the guaranteed time to acknowledge an incident?
00:07:04 Jordan: For Priority 1 incidents we acknowledge within 15 minutes — that's part of our Dedicated SLA; for hosted tier it's typically 60 minutes for non-paid tiers but we'll spell that out.
00:07:16 Samira: Good. Who signs off on a public incident notification? Do you coordinate with our comms?
00:07:22 Priya: We coordinate. We provide draft notifications and time the announcement with customers. For Dedicated, you'll have a joint comms plan.
00:07:30 Luis: Any limitations on data residency during failover? If primary EU region goes down and you failover to us-east-1, that violates residency.
00:07:37 Alex: We support region-locked failover policies. For EU-only tenants we will failover to a secondary EU region. For Private on-prem we don't cross borders unless explicitly configured. We'll include the policy matrix.
00:07:51 Samira: Ok good. Let's capture actionables.
00:07:53 Jordan: Quick recap: Jordan to send SOC2/ISO, Priya to send architecture + KMS flow, Alex to include uptime metrics and sample restore postmortem, Acme to send incident runbook and confirm residency constraints, and schedule tabletop exercise.
00:08:07 Tom: We'll put forward dates — week of May 5 is fine.
00:08:11 Nina (Compliance): Also confirm audit log immutability options and retention for EU data.
00:08:16 Priya: Noted — will include S3 write-once options and SIEM streaming details.
00:08:22 Samira: Thank you — this was helpful.
00:08:25 Jordan: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts and get the tabletop on the calendar.
00:08:29 [end of call]
